title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference 10.19.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: like where's your head at stuff like this? And when you get to a game like this, are you are you really dwelling on the stuff that you have to fix? Are you trying to like keep uh glass half full kind of look with it? >> Win or lose, I mean, you're just trying to coach these guys, you know? So, I mean, yeah, the the easy answer is you you love coaching after a win and and and sometimes guys are a little bit more receptive, but um at this level in this league, um you got to have thick skin on Mondays, good or bad, you know. Uh we're a field goal miss away from not feeling this way. Uh we were 12 feet away two weeks before. We didn't get it done. We felt like we should have. We didn't, you know, and it's just like you can't live in those those highs and lows and you just from a coaching standpoint, all we can do is provide the clarity to them, coach them up as hard as we can and um you know, try to improve. >> How did Walt come out with the anchor? >> Um okay, we'll know a little bit more. I'll give you guys a little bit more update uh Wednesday or Thursday. >> You're watching the film. What do you think really kind of initiated the defensive performance yesterday? >> Yeah, I thought um I thought their play style was was awesome. Um it looked to me like they had clear minds. I I just saw clear minds. I saw 11 as one. I saw cleats in the ground. Um and uh I thought they were just working together in in unison. It was uh it was really cool. It was reminiscent of of what I felt like I saw in 24, maybe even in the early parts of last year. Um in terms of just something that did not look fun for the opposing offense. Uh cuz I know uh you know like I've said to you guys, I know there were times in um 24 that it was not fun having to go against this squad and and that that's what it looked like to me and and hopefully we uh you know are even better than that. >> What went into the conversations this week to kind of bring back some of that aggression and bring back some of those looks from 24 that you mentioned. >> Well, I mean I'm going to keep some of that in house if you if you don't mind for obvious reasons um because we're still trying to if this was the last game of the year then yeah then maybe I'd answer that. But uh you know there's um it was good. It was it was all productive and uh you know now it's hey they they that's their standard. They set the bar right there. That was a that was a really good defensive performance. And um you know sometimes when an offense struggles you know obviously LA is going to clean up their stuff. I'm not in their meetings obviously right now. But a lot of times it's because the defense made it hard on you too. You know and uh I mean I think about all the all the tape I've watched of Denver already. like it's going to be really really difficult cuz their defense makes it really really hard you know and so I thought our defense did that yesterday said he was squeamish playing that defense I mean you've been around Stafford >> what does squeamish mean easy I would say >> I mean is that the tone you guys want to set >> yeah I mean I just want to play great defense and I want like I want hair on fire hats to the ball shots on the ball um 11 is one and that's that's what I saw yesterday and um the guys should be proud of that performance they put out there. It was it was real. And again, I one of my favorite things I told these guys this is win or lose, I I love going home and watching the TV copy, just sitting there with my wife and kids and and re-watching it just to see kind of what you guys are seeing or what the fans are seeing or whatnot and and um cuz I think the tape can do the talking, you know, and you could see that play style yesterday. >> Watch uh get going yesterday. >> Yeah, it was cool. You know, he was uh he was a force on the edge there and obviously um you know, had the production um you know to uh to boot with it. So, um, it it was good. >> Looking at the red zone, was there a central issue that you found was the problem? >> Yeah, we we weren't efficient in our runs, um, you know, at all down there. Uh, so, uh, obviously got to do a better job of scheming some stuff up right there. But, uh, you know, I thought we had great efficiency from the 20s to 20s all day. Um, I don't think I mean, we did. It's just when we got inside the 20. Obviously, we know that's not sustainable. We can't kick six field goals and expect to win football games. Um, but uh, you know, I I think those are those are um, I don't want to call them easy fixes because there are no easy fixes, but I mean we'll we'll clean that up. >> You guys seem to you guys seem to use significantly more motion than you had all season and you find a little bit more success on those looks or were you able to kind of unlock off those plays? >> Um, I feel like we've been motioning quite a bit, I guess. I mean, I know you you'll probably have all the numbers on that, but uh, um, you know, again, we we we motion for a reason. we don't just motion to motion and sometimes the reason is just to change up a look or obviously uh give our guys leverages and advantages and stuff like that. So, um but uh yeah, I mean that's all that was to move the ball as well as you did and sustain drives that long when you get into the red zone. Is it really just a difference of the shorter field and the tighter windows or is there something more challenging about that part of the field in particular that would maybe be an answer for the difference from the rest? Yeah, I mean, well, I mean, when you when you can use the the back end line as kind of the 12th defender, I mean, it it takes 75% of your offense out for every team because you're obviously not going to be working as much play action, stuff like that. Like, you you don't have as much space. But, uh, you know, again, [snorts] that I don't want to say it really hasn't been a problem this year. I mean, we've been I think we were going into the game, we were like 13th in the red zone or something like that, which is not great. We want to be number one uh for obvious reasons. uh we're going to take a pretty step back uh from from uh that ranking now going 0 for five, but uh I know um I know our guys uh know ways that we we can get this figured out. >> Following up on the uh the idea of the longer drives, how much of you guys holding the ball and, you know, having that possession, how much do you think that helps the defense? Yeah, I mean anytime you can keep the defense off the field as much as as we did there. You think about the games um you know that that we've played well if you will. I mean the Chargers this game um San Francisco I mean we our guys played well in that game. Um we are killing ourselves with the penalties and then obviously the penalty stopped in the second half but we controlled the ball. Um, obviously their offense in San Francisco, you know, that was a tough day for us, but um, you know, that's that's kind of somewhat starting to be our identity a little bit in terms of when we're playing good ball. It's long sustained drives. Again, it's it's not easy doing what they're doing out there going on 15 play drives and and you know, I think we had two drives of over eight minutes or something like that or eight and a half minutes. I mean, that's it's insane, but it's kind of what we're doing right now. And um you know, as long as we're we're being efficient and and we're executing um you know, you don't force an identity, you just you know, you're going to have your foundations. But again, like I've said about us in LA last year, didn't run a uh a 13 personnel snap until week six. Then we kind of figured out what our identity was. Um we're going into, you know, week seven now and I I think we're um starting to kind of figure out what works for us. Um still would obviously love to be more explosive. Hasn't happened yet, but it's still early in the season. Does [snorts] your play calling philosophy change at all inside the red zone? And if so, how and to what degree does it change? >> Well, it's kind of like I was saying, I mean, you're you're limited in which obviously you can call. I mean, you're not going to be calling long shots because you can't right there, you know. So, um you know, it's there's a lot of factors that go into it. Uh defenses change. You got to figure out where kind of their cut off is. Is it the 15 yard line? Is it the 12 yardd line? When are some of those field pressures going to um stop showing up? when are they going to start bringing some of the red zone pressure? So, I mean, there's a there's a cat and mouse game to it as well, you know, but ultimately when we get in there, we just got to finish finish the job. >> With all the injuries that you guys had at safety, what went into the decision to slide Garrett over there? And what does it say about his skill set that he's able to >> Yeah, he's doing he's he's doing a good job over there. He's a he's a smart football player. Um, you know, so it's not You'd have to ask him, but it doesn't seem like it's it's too big of a transition for him. Um, you know, mentally and uh and physically. So, he's doing a good job back there. and um you know it's u he's been an asset for us. >> You mentioned the penalties and how that affects the team operation wise. What did you see as far as attention to detail as far as how the guys were able to execute those things that take no talent in that final drive? >> Um yeah, no, they they they did a great job. I mean the I can't remember exactly how many penalties I've I've already kind of moved on to Denver as you guys probably can tell, but um you know didn't have many penalties uh throughout the day. had the one um obviously when we threw that screen we were in illegal formation. I I blame that on me. They they subbed late. We were in we were in 13. They were in dime. Then they subbed back to base and so then I changed the play and and I know I was frantically trying to get it in before 15 seconds. And when you do that just voice complexion I it affects the quarterback and then the quarterback says it probably a little faster than he wanted to. And um you know so I put that one on me because it just was I got the play call in late and that's that's what happens. But uh you know when you do that usually um you know bad things do happen. But um I thought I thought for the most part our operation was pretty clean throughout the day and um you know when we needed it there at the end they got it done. >> You mentioned you mentioned just a few minutes ago about how when you were in LA 13 personnel week six for the last two weeks the 13th personnel usage here has continued to go up. Is that becoming this team's identity now? >> I think it's uh it's it's certainly helped us. you know, we got um tight ends and I thought you saw a little bit more with Elijah. Obviously, Tegan had the two touchdowns the week before. Um I think you guys all know what Trey can do. Um so, you got you got different uh skill sets that these guys can provide for us, not just in the run game, but in the pass game as well. And um be able to present, you know, some of those formations u or some of some of that 13 personnel, not just u old school, you know, all all guys hands in the dirt, but spread it out a little bit and and you know, give the defense a few wrinkles. Last week we were, you know, talking about Nick's job status and you were obviously very confident in him and that he turns in this performance, you know, from the defense. Why why were you so confident in him? Why do you think he was able to bounce back with this? >> Yeah, I I trust the human. I trust the worker. I know I know what the players think of him. Um, you know, and uh obviously we know this is a resultsbased business. We we understand that. we know that, you know, but uh I I just I I knew our our defense had more than what we'd been putting out there and we we just had to unlock it some way somehow. And again, this was just one week. Uh but it was a step in the right direction. And I and I do believe we can grow from this one. Um I do believe we can start to build an identity off of this one. Um each week's going to be, you know, a game of its own and and there's always going to be unique challenges, but uh um I got uh I got a lot of faith in Nick. I got a lot of faith in the rest of the defensive staff. I think they're coaching their butt off. I think the details are improving. Um, I think you could see that yesterday, particularly out front. Um, you know, and and I think, uh, like I said, I I believe in the players that have to go out and execute it. >> People say that that field goals is the kicker's basic job, right? But what did you see like when that has to work six times, when that has to that mechanism has to function six times properly to to be successful? What are you seeing in that to that led to it functioning properly? >> Saw the same thing you saw six kicks go right up the middle. So, I don't know how to coach a kicker. I never will. So, um I just try to stay out of their way. Um but no, I you know, the operation looks smooth. I mean, there's there's a lot that has to go into it. I mean, is it is the the dirtiest, you know, one and a half seconds or whatever our line calls it. Um it is a thankless job having to block for those. Obviously, the snap's got to be right. The hold's got to be right. The kicker's got to have the right mindset. Um and uh you know, he knocked them in yesterday. >> Those pin and pull runs that you guys have had been really [snorts] effective. It's not something at least last year you guys did it all in LA. What is it with this group that seems to be you've found some so much success with that? >> Yeah, it's um it's been a good good change up for us obviously cuz uh you're under center, you can do some of that those perimeter runs. Um they've done that here for a few years. Something that uh Fry is um you know really coached dating back to college. Uh we used to do quite a bit of it in San Francisco back um in 2019 when we had like Kevin Coleman and Matt Breita um Jeff Wilson Raheem Oster that was a big big part of our scheme and then kind of um you know when I went to New York didn't didn't do it too much and then in LA didn't do it. So it's been it's been a few years it's been fun to kind of dive back into that but again it's like one of those things you um you want to get good at something like I don't believe in doing everything every run scheme. I just think you know like what are you actually good at? But I do think it's been a good change up for us uh based on some of the other stuff we want to do in the run game. >> What did you think of Ban just stepping in and just showing up like he did on Sunday? >> Yeah, not shocking. He's a he's a stud. He's a tough dude. He's a tough tackle. Um you know, so uh that I've seen it in a green jersey over in New York and then got to see it obviously uh yesterday. So yeah, he ran hard. I thought the guys did a great job. I thought everyone was connected. We have a lot to clean up in the run game. Obviously, we hit some of those, you know, G series like you're talking about right there, but um we uh we got a lot to clean up with our downhill direct runs, but they, you know, they still were getting dirty. Two, three yard runs um when they wasn't, you know, necessarily executed. >> What is the key to cleaning up some of those down and down runs? >> Yeah, we got uh won't uh totally get into it, but I talked to the staff about it today and uh you know, got some uh some different ideas on how to clean that stuff up. >> Are there any uh coaching points on LJ's return? What would you do? >> Like he could have maybe tossed it. >> But is that the the right thing to do in that two-point conversion? >> Absolutely. It is right. >> So I I don't know if he still believes that. U we'll coach that on Friday in our situation uh meeting because that won't happen in practice obviously. But uh you know if that's if that was um a non two-point conversion then I mean you see people do it. But I've also seen it go haywire when you're trying to, you know, a D lineman trying to, you know, give a ball to a to a DB or whatnot. But, uh, I've seen it worked. I I've seen it not work. And two-point conversion, it's basically a no risk. Give it give it to the fast guy. LJ was rolling, though. >> How make sure that your guys are prepared for like that's such a niche situation, right? It's going to happen on a two like how there's so many plays like that in football that can happen. So many niche situations. How do you make sure your guys are prepared for every random? Yeah, it's well it's it's a good question because I I I'm not a believer in giving them the 0.00001enters. I just like I want to get good at running duo. I want to get good at playing cover four. I want to get good at our techniques. I want to be do good at the the 99% stuff, not the 1%. Some people would disagree with me on that. That's just um honestly that's just kind of the way that that I've been brought up in the NFL with guys like Kyle and Shawn and stuff like that. Like we want to get good at the at the basic stuff, not not that kind of stuff. So, but organically, uh, those can things can happen to your team. That obviously happened yesterday. Um, and then on Friday, we just kind of show around the league, kind of keep it a little bit light, if you will, um, and have some levity in those meetings a little bit. Uh, on the Friday, showing what's kind of going around in the league if we're in this situation. Uh, this is how we would do it from a coaching staff, uh, standpoint, how we would do it from a situational standpoint, and then just players just kind of seeing what, you know, what's going on. Do >> you [snorts] copy every week? And if you do, what's it like to hear kind of the announcers, their opinions, kind of what they think of everything? What's it like? >> Um, I I I don't really care about what they're saying. Um, no disrespect to them. It's more just like I just want to see kind of what we look like, you know, and I've uh because again you're you're down there, you're in the moment and then you're going to watch the the silent copy, but I also like to just kind of, you know, there's things that you can see in the TV copy that you don't see necessarily in the silent copy because of obviously all the cameras and stuff like that, like Trey screaming at sidelines and and all those kind of things. Like you don't really you don't really see that u you know on the uh on the silent copy. you were joking about, you know, not knowing anything about how to kick field goals, but what is the head coach's job when it comes to kickers or punters, you know, stuff that you don't necessarily specialize in, but are obviously very important? >> Yeah, I just I I trust the people that know what they're doing in those situations, like our special teams coordinator, like uh like Monty. Um I mean, we you know, like obviously I have to have a baseline understanding of what's going on. Like can the guy kick or can he can he punt well? opinion like I mean it's not I'm not going to and it's hard to do the job that they do obviously but I mean I think we all can see the good kickers the good punters people out kicking their coverage in the punting units and all those kind of things but uh no I I I that's above my pay grade [snorts] lose their kicker as early as they did and that obviously impacted how aggressive they were kind of playing chess calling a game does that impact some of the decisions you're making >> you know I it did for Nick for sure because obviously, you know, u especially in the first half, you knew they were just playing for touchdowns and then uh obviously we knew that they were out there at halftime trying to work uh with their punter, you know, getting some kicks and I guess he obviously he was kicking it well enough where they where they uh kicked the extra point there and uh to take the lead. But uh we were just trying to play our game on offense, you know, and um be as efficient as as possible, keep our defense off the field, which we did. And like we talked about, I mean, it was a good day up until we got inside the 20. And um you know, I'll uh like I said, we'll we'll get that cleaned up. >> Did you uh partake in the victory hot dogs today? >> No, I didn't. I saw it up there, but no, I did not.

title: Ravens Brace Themselves as Lamar Jackson Return Questions Swirl
text: It's week seven and it is Bengals week in Baltimore. But a lot to review from week six Sunday in Cleveland. That and a whole lot more coming up inside the collective tonight. Glad you're with us. It is Tuesday and it is 8:00 sharp. The 20th of October. Week seven begins today and the Ravens and Bengals will square off in Baltimore on Sunday at 1:00. Our friend Cole Jackson will be with us momentarily. I'm Bobby Tet. This is Jeff Zerbeck of The Athletic, of course. Great to have you guys with us. If you could like the video on your way in, we would appreciate it. Subscribe to the channel if you haven't already done so. Hit that notification bell for future purposes. We'll get to as many Q&A super chats as we can as they come in. And thanks to all of our sponsors, Prize Picks, SeatGeek, and the folks at Blueprint, a brand new one, Jez Rebec, which we'll get into in just a bit. But you see the docket on the lefth hand side. We'll go through everything. All eyes being on Lamar. U we got to get of course a new to I'm just realizing we we didn't have a two show planned. So that docket on the lefth hand side for topics is outdated. Don't you worry once Cole gets in we'll get the the new one up to snuff. But obviously it begins with all eyes on Lamar Jackson just as it has been the last two weeks Jeff since he went down in that Titans game. So uh all eyes for tomorrow's practice including yours uh once that media portion begins. will will certainly be relevant tomorrow. >> Yeah. Each week that passes by without him practicing on the field kind of adds another practice day he's going to have to take part in for you know for me to kind of be comfortable in saying yeah he's going to play this Sunday for example like he hasn't been he hasn't been on the field now in basically two and a half weeks. So I don't think this is something where you can just practice lightly on Thursday Friday to be ready to play. He's missed a good bit of time. So, I think he needs some semblance of a full practice week to be able to play Sunday. It doesn't necessarily mean he has to be on the field Wednesday, but there has to be some level of engagement um with him uh for much of this week in terms of being on that field, I think, to get a a good sense that he's going to play. And look, I talked to someone early last week. They thought he was going to be practicing and play. that didn't happen. Now people aren't even saying anything at this point. It's just like there is no expectation. I I have no expectation, good, bad, or indifferent. Um and really, you know, I think we've seen based on some of these reports, Bobby, nationally particular, that no one really knows anything. And this is the world we live in with Lamar. Uh ultimately, it's his call. When he feels right, when he's ready to play, he'll be out there. Um, and I'm sure he's, you know, all reports are that or all indications are he's he's been working hard trying to get back, but the injury certainly has lingered now. And, um, we'll see uh, where we're at this week. I don't mean to be Debbie Downer, but it would be tough to feel good about their chances to beat the Bengals if Lamar Jackson's not on the on not on the field. >> Cincy's coming off a buy. Buffalo will be coming off a buy the following week when they host the Ravens at their new stadium. Will that game still be a one o'clock start? We'll wait and see. I know you and I were perplexed by that back in May when the schedule came out. >> Yeah. And I mean, look, after watching that, you know, the Eagles and the Commanders and the Cowboys. I mean, I'm sure the NFL would love to flex that game for the following Sunday and get what is it? It's Eagles Washington the following Sunday, I think. I'm sure they would love to get that game off, especially now, no Herz, no Terry Mcccluren, um, two teams who are really struggling, but I just don't think you can move the Ravens game to a night game because you have the Thursday night game the following week. Asking the Ravens to play a Sunday night game on the road where they wouldn't get into Baltimore in the wee hours of Monday morning and having them come back and playing a Thursday night game. That's unfair, right? I I I don't see how they could do that. I know there's some speculation that they may move the Browns and Steelers into the Sunday night game, which would be interesting. Uh Good Feather and Todd Monkin's cap that they're playing well enough to warrant a prime time flex. We'll see how that happens. Um but you know, the big game that's with that week looks like Chiefs Broncos, but my guess is that's the one in the 425 slot that CBS really wants to hold there. Well, and speaking of, you know, you mentioned Todd, he's a firsttime head coach, as is Jesse, and everybody's looking up at Joe Brady in Buffalo in terms of how first year through the first six weeks of the season, how firstear head coaches have fared. Uh, the Bills are five- one. Ravens find themselves among three teams with firstear coaches who are 4-2 along with Pittsburgh and Cleveland. Now, is Mike a first Mike McCarthy a first year head coach? No. But he's in year one with Pittsburgh. And you see the rest the way that the rest of this is shaken out, including John Harbaugh's Giants 3-2 and one. They made some news today by cutting the former Steeler Naji Harris. That's gotten awfully interesting. But your thoughts through the first six weeks of Jesse Mter's tenure. is probably coming off, yeah, sour taste in the fan base's mouth based on how that final quarter went in Cleveland, but overall output-wise, probably their best defensive performance in totality through the first six weeks of the season. >> Yeah, I I I'm doing a a grades piece. Uh um Bobby was assigned. I'm not big on grade, you know, like it's once something was suggested and I'm all for it. I know people liked interactive stuff. And I had a little hard time grading the coaching staff because in one sense they've lost two games that they had no business losing. And I think in this case um you know I don't I think there were some coaching blunders in the New Orleans Saints game. I he blew a challenge the Declan Doyle. um they've been a heavily penalized team which you know doesn't necessarily affect well on the coaching staff but you look at all the other factors it's like they've been ready to play uh for the most part they he the coaching staff's really won the the the locker room over there's been a lot of belief there um so I think for the most part I I give him pretty high marks um and uh you know everything you know he's pretty much been as advertised But you can't sugarcoat that. Lost Sunday. You just can't. And I know, you know, like a couple people had reached out to me, fans, regular readers that thought I was way negative in my story off Sunday's game. Um, and and maybe I was, but I mean, that's again, it's just a game you cannot lose. like if it was a good team or like um I I don't I don't want to say the Browns aren't good, but let look the Browns defense is good, but they're missing most of their defensive line. They're one of their best players. Grant Delpit gets hurt and misses all but like the second all but the first drive. So, they're banged up badly defensively. Offensive offensively, they were a mess. That that's just the game. I don't care that Tyler Huntley's uh was in at quarterback. They had plenty in all three phases where they should have handled that team and they didn't get the job done. That's a bad loss. You could say what you want, but that's a bad loss. And that's one of these losses where you're looking at in December when you have to go on the road and beat a really good football team. Um and you're saying, "Wow, I wish we hadn't dropped that game." So, um it doesn't have to define their season. it doesn't have to linger, but given what they had ahead of them, this gauntlet of three games, one of them's on a short week and they're playing the team on a short week that's a week removed from the buy. The other two are against teams who are going to be fresh off the buy. The Bengals, I think I read, have pretty much every player on the practice field ready to go except maybe one. It's just a really tough spot. And you go into that five and one, you have some margin of error. If you drop one or two of those games, you're still sitting pretty through nine games at, you know, maybe six and three. And I think you feel good about that. But everything changes when you lose that game. And and you know, I don't maybe, as I said, maybe it was a bit negative, but that's just a game you can't lose. I I don't care that Tyler Huntley's your quarterback. Um Tyler Huntley, they were up 10 nothing. They're in control of the game. They just did not get enough. The offense was terrible in the fourth quarter. special teams was terrible in the fourth quarter and after dominating the game, the defense let down in the fourth quarter. I mean, the Browns basically had three scoring drives in their last in the fourth quarter. The guy missed a field goal and one, but that's unacceptable against that offense and somebody needed to make a play and again they didn't make the play. So, I don't think I was overly negative. I just think it was a really bad loss. >> It was a bad loss. Like, yeah, Tyler Huntley was Tyler Huntley's not a great quarterback and he was specifically bad in this game. He's probably what a mid-tier backup quarterback relative to other backups in the league, but this was a game like obviously the focus is on the injuries Baltimore is facing like Lamar Jackson obviously huge loss. That's not groundbreaking analysis. The Browns were missing several key players and had a guy like Carson Swessinger who's their best defensive player who yes, he played but he he didn't look himself. He didn't he looked a step slow. uh that front seven was beat up and they basically said, "Hey, Tyler Huntley's going to have to pop a one or two over our head and Huntley wasn't able to do it. I don't think outside of like the reality is a lot of their gains of the 235 yards and one touchdown they scored." A couple of them were pretty gimmicky. You know, they they have the play where it's fun. They have Josh Quavos lined up at left guard and he takes it for 27. But that's not like your normal offense, right? Like this was a game where I wanted this team to be able to come out and pound the rock, set up play action, simple, keep it simple, set up like a game manager role for Tyler Huntley. They weren't able to run the football outside of three big gains. They they they basically ran for one or two yards every time they ran the football. Uh some of that was alignment based, but I think I I I put, you know, a lot of it on Declan Doyle to be completely honest. He seemed scared to run the ball inside. He basically only ran it to the edges. And as soon as the Browns started hanging out in the overhang and and bringing their edges a little bit wider and crashing down, they didn't have any answers. They basically were successful on one zone toss and one two trap plays. That that was it. That was the whole run game. So, you know, he didn't trust this. And again, like this is sometimes your offensive coordinator is limited by what the offensive line is going to give them. But I expected more out of this offense. even with Tyler Huntley, you know, we and he missed throws, so I mean, that's on his execution, but they just they look like they didn't have a game plan. Um, I think it was one of the biggest disappointments that I saw was just how woefully unprepared Declan Doyle seemed for this game. And it reminds you of some of like he's he's a he's a young coach. We saw some of that um youth show in the Saints game and we saw it, I think, again, on Sunday. >> Yeah. My biggest issue, Bobby, is it just feels like one step forward, two steps back. title: Zac Taylor Press Conference - October 19
text: All right. Far away. >> Are there any injuries coming out of our this week? I know that Dobbs was back. What's the status of the guys that have been out? >> Yeah. Yeah, I think he's progressing along and so we'll kind of see where he's at. >> What about Cassius Marsh? >> Sick. >> He's sick? >> Yeah. >> Coach, what was the what was the kind of the What did you do as a coaching staff during the bye that What were the What was kind of on the agenda or everything that you wanted to check off going into this week? >> Couple things. Obviously, they got new schemes, but um there's still a lot of similarities from from the past. They got great players, great coaching staff. Um it's exciting. I think our guys really get fired up for this game. He's got a lot of confidence. I think the players respect him and have confidence in him. Did a great job when he was with the Chargers. You know, we played them a couple of years ago. So, you you you can just tell he's somebody in the industry that has always been well thought of and players have always had respect for him and so it's no surprise that he's he's jumped right into the fray and is doing well over there. >> With Tannehill, with that Tannehill going out, do you think Evan will uh uh does he get more of a you know, more reps in the passing game, more targets? >> I think you know, we'll call on the the whole room in the receiver room. We're getting healthy at the receiver room, too. So, I think just combining both those rooms and dispersing how those roles will play out is is something we're always open to week-to-week. You know, we feel like we've got a lot of people with a lot of different strengths um that can all play at a high level in both those rooms and just find ways to game plan for those guys to get them all involved is important for us. >> You know, you've talked a lot about Eric's physicality and his and his what he does in the running game play, but he's kind of a sneaky YAC guy after the catch. >> Sure. Yeah, he's physical players. I think when he's got the ball in his hands he looks to bring that physicality and and try to get what he can after the catch. >> Is that Chester a potential candidate to come back on the 53? >> We'll see. We'll keep working out all those guys that are on IR and and seeing how they're progressing. >> You had him on on your side for the past couple of years. How difficult is it to scheme against Trey? >> He's a good player, you know, and so again, they got a lot of good players on their defense and we got to put together a great plan and be able to execute it to give ourselves the best chance to win. >> Kobe Young, can he be back in the mix and maybe you talked about the role he could he had before his injury, can he reassume that or >> I think so. Yeah. Yeah, he's looked as good as he's looked in a long time. You know, I think last week he had a good week on on what he can handle from a rehab perspective. Um so this week to get him back involved, he looked good running around today. So I think it's good to to finally get him back and feel like he's he's closer to 100% health. >> How similar is some of the stuff your bigger receivers do to what Tanner does? Like not that they're interchangeable, do they do a lot of similar stuff? >> Yes and no. you know, you you do put them in a little bit different position when they're not playing wide. Like Tanner plays sometimes, he can only play in F for us. And so that role is very similar to what our receivers are doing. so it doesn't, you know, to lose Tanner and get Colby back in some ways does help. Because in some ways they they can they can play some similar roles in some situations. >> Brian Cook played [clears throat] in a couple of these games, missed a couple. How much of a difference have you noticed kind of when he's out there, good things seem to happen? >> Yeah, I think he feels a lot better now. You know, coming off the bye week, moving around today, watching him move around. Um I think the confidence of being closer to 100% I I I hate to put a percentage on him, but I I think he feels a lot better than he probably did 2 weeks ago, 3 weeks ago. And um so it's good to get him back closer to full strength. >> How big can his tackling, just his all that stuff be against Baltimore when you look >> I I think big time. You know, it's yeah, they're they're obviously backs who are very physical players. Um quarterback, whoever plays, you know, is is obviously elusive. And so you got to be sure tacklers and um the communication's got to be a big part of it, you know, with with just the way that they formulate their offense and and try to tackle you. That's a big key of it. So I think having a veteran player back there can can help with all that. >> With the with the early bye and knowing you're not going to have another break until maybe a possible playoff bye, does it change your approach on how you handle guys' workload, you know, coming down the second half? >> Not necessarily in the games, no. I mean we're going to do everything we can to win. Does it change the workload during practice? Potentially. I think we've done a good job of that so far during the season with with some of the guys that are more veteran. Um so we're never shy away from helping guys during the week that maybe don't need the physical reps and and we need them healthy on Sunday. Um, obviously strange weeks coming coming forward at us and so we'll do a great job just with the schedule and try to keep it off these guys best we can. >> Do you feel like at this point of the season you've got a good good sense of what your identity is on offense? >> Yes. >> What do you what do you if there's a way to kind of verbalize that, what do you feel like that >> Trying to put ourselves in a great position to score points on every drive. That's that's our number one key right now. >> I know you guys take like a five-week approach and you don't look past your opponent, but how often do you when you're presenting to the team write out like the division rankings? >> Occasionally. You know, um, not every week, but I think it is take a snapshot of where things are across the across the the league. but do I do it every week? No, but I don't think there's there's anything negative to it when you just show, "Hey, here's where we're at, you know, and maybe it can be awful lot sometimes, you know, early in the season like, "Yeah, it feels feels bad right now, but here's where we are in relation to everybody else." It takes one week to change that narrative, change how you feel, put yourself right back in the thick of things. So, I think that's our focus right now is just go on the road, tremendous opportunity to go on the road versus a great team, uh, find a way to get a win and and put yourself in a good position. So, um, but if we don't focus on the details all week, then none of that's going to matter. So, I I think these guys they understand that. We've said that over and over again. But, I am excited to go on the road, uh, tremendous opportunity right in front of us. Again, I think with two great teams play each other, it's always it always makes for a fun game and um, so look forward to the week of prep and see how we end up on Sunday. >> Talk about talk about going on the road in the division. I I the last time you played these guys in the light of day >> Never. Never. >> [laughter] >> 21? >> Five years ago, which was a which was a big game really in in in the life of this franchise really. I mean, that was kind of you know, Burrow had a bust out so did Jamar. I mean, what do you remember about that game? >> Seven-man protection. That was our first game we introduced seven-man protection, you know, and and Cali. I remember I remember a lot about that week and Samaje had a big run at the end of the game kind of icing for a minute. Um but yeah, that was the last time I think I've seen daylight in Baltimore. So yeah, this [clears throat] is this feels a little different. >> But how significant of a of a win was that? Do you think that kind of moved a lot for your team? >> I think it absolutely. You know, we hadn't really won uh I guess we won at Pittsburgh that year before that. But um they had been the team, you know, at that moment in time. I think they'd probably won the last two year 2019 to 20. So it's hard to go back all that, but yeah, I think that was significant one for us to um win there, which we hadn't done in two years and get on the plane and enjoy that and um it was probably at the point in the year where it was good to get a win like that to our guys to to verify the confidence they had. You know, we we we thought we were a good team and it kind of solidified that for us. Now, we had to go play a bunch of other games after that, but um yeah, that was that was a big game for us back then. That was one of the bigger games I think we've ever won in my time here. >> Does your team need that now? Verifying the confidence. >> think so. I I think cuz we've now played enough games, but that team that was still a relatively young team for for us for just probably age-wise in general. Um so I think there's there's years and moments where you need that stuff. I I don't think this is a team that has to have that. Um I really want it, but but I I don't know that it's the same position that we were in back in >> What made Jack Kaiser a good fit with Swasey out? >> Somebody we'd always had our eye on, you know, dating back to the draft and um got taken in Jacksonville before, you know before it came to us and obviously he's got got good rapport with several of the guys on our staff so he understands the defense able to come in there so you got a guy that you know can can come and fit in immediately somebody we've always liked somebody who's got a relationship with our staff someone who's who's tape we've always liked when he's been in the league so it works out well and we're we're happy to have him. >> Looking forward to week 10 the key is getting more explosive than maybe you've had so far this season. >> Um just I mean QB and retail and again just just trying to get points on the board. >> Thanks coach.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald: "I’m Excited About Where We Can Go" | Seattle Seahawks
text: Had a Had a great day today. After uh after a break. Some longer for some than others, but uh I think we're all able to be out of here yesterday and have good family time, so that was great. And we had a great day today and looking forward to get back to our process on on Wednesday and getting rolling. >> You mentioned that you were going to have a conversation with Sam and Jake and and Bryan Fury. Did that conversation happen? And And was Cooper Kupp part of that conversation as well? >> Um it wasn't just like one conversation. There's a There We had We had a lot of conversations over the last uh few days. Coop's uh Coop's a part of that. Um Coop's a tremendous asset for us, so we want uh we want all those guys to feel like we're all part of the solution and how we're going to move forward, so um Coop's been great. >> How do you feel those conversations went compared to what you expected? >> Yeah, I I I think I think, you know, what we've told the team today is you kind of you you end a game The games are so emotional, you know, you leave a game and you're and you um I guess the emotions do vary sometimes from week to week based off the game. I think I think uh where our where my frustration lie was just I I think we talked about this after the game was just the identity of us and what it feels like, you know, Seahawk Seahawk football and um that feeling wasn't there. And so you you know, you you have frustration, but with that your your frustration about with also without the facts and like without the like the objectivity behind everything. So, I think that's what's that's what makes the the you know, the the the kind of the problems solving process uh interesting. It makes I mean, that's part of the reason we like being coaches cuz that's part of our process, so um I'm proud of the the days you know, the couple days work that we put in. I think that we had some some honest conversations and honest process. Um I think we're I think we're definitely more aligned as a team than we were a few days ago and uh I'm excited about where we can go, honestly. I mean but you know, we've really had one good days of work work worth of work up to this point. So, it's it's it's a matter of following through and and making sure we're hitting the checkpoints on a daily basis just like it was before. but uh but it was definitely I think it was definitely a couple days like well served. So, uh I think this is cause for excitement on where we can go. >> On the identity not being where you want it to be, is it as simple as the turnovers or is there more to it than that? >> Yeah, again, I I I think I think when you're when you look at like, "Hey, there's line items of throughout all three phases of our team that we want to get better at." Well, you know, those are those are symptoms of things that were are within our control that we can we can be better, you know, so like the example I like to use is tackling. It's like, "Well, we're not tackling well." Well, not cuz the guys don't want to tackle. It's probably because there's too much space. It's probably because there's a fundamental that maybe we could have worked better, the guy could have applied better to that type of situation or maybe it's more effort coming from a certain angle or maybe it's an angle we need to take. So, it's more fundamental things that we want to be able to you know, like apply in those situations that we can hit those are things that we can handle here throughout the week so they got we feel like our players are better trained to go tackle better. Which if we tackle great, then you're going to everyone's >> going to say, "Hey man, their plan is great." >> Seahawk defense. Well, cuz their fundamentals are on point, you know, so um hopefully that kind of paints you a picture about what we feel like can slow down the the takeaway issue. >> Are are there things like schematically as well that you feel like you need to I don't know change or kind of discuss in this as well what you're doing? >> Uh I think short answer is yes. The long answer is um Are we running bad plays? Are we No, no, our play the plays are fine. It's it's It's how we get to the plays. It's how we run the plays. How we choose the plays. How we execute the plays, those type of things. >> When we all notice the results on the field, but Sam Darnold [clears throat] since he's come back, his leadership for the locker room, how was How do you assess that since his injury? >> Sam's been great. Sam's been great. All the things that we said that we were always impressed by Sam was his consistency and his attitude his kind of just like a ball player attitude, like every day same guy. Sam's been um very consistent. He's been been trying to be part of the conversations of us and on where we can go. So, he's been he's been great. >> He was wearing it pretty heavy with us in Denver after the game. Did you notice any frustration or difference in him than any other game? >> I think we're all heavy and frustrated. So. >> What is What is chances obviously Anthony Bradford got activated I think he's going to get activated. >> Yeah. >> Chances that he plays this week and and what what is it going to mean potentially to have him back? >> I know normally I'm pretty quiet on this one, but it's pretty straightforward. If he has a good week, he's going to he's going to play a significant amount if not the whole game. So, uh it's exciting. I think uh I think AB really I'm I'm really really happy for AB like the way he's approached this injury and how he's how he's um really stayed I think he's I think he's a better version of himself than he was um before he got injured. So, I think that just speaks to his work ethic and his positive mentality, which is really really cool. So, um AB's played really good football for us. He's a physical presence for us at right guard. Uh both in run and pass. So, uh we're excited to to possibly get him back. >> What What's the situation with Elijah Royal? >> Uh yeah, Elijah he's um he's going to be out a significant amount of time. How long that is, I'm not not sure. Uh, there's some options on the table that I think we're just about finalized, but without putting anybody in a bad spot, I think that's the best way to describe it right now. >> Is it safe to say he's going on IR? >> That's what I'm saying. Like, it's I could say that, but then you never know between now and when I know for sure, so I'll I'll know more on Wednesday. >> I think that I guess the daily Zach Charbonnet question if if he's uh, he's >> Yeah, thanks. >> [laughter] >> This wasn't the first question, but uh, Zach is um, he's going to have a uh, a full week's worth of reps. So, that's exciting and uh, there's a possibility that you could see him on Sunday uh, in some capacity, so that's that's exciting. >> How about Jake Darian? Any updates on him? >> Uh, no update on JD. I think uh, I think we got one more game and then we'll go from there, but >> [clears throat] >> no update on JD. He's doing well, though. >> Is it a shoulder for a royal? >> A shoulder for a royal, I believe, yeah. >> Whether Zach plays this week or not, just the work he's done to go from a surgery in February to even being in this conversation in October. >> Yeah, yeah, it's remarkable. Um, I know he's had a certain date in mind, which is a really ambitious date and uh, and for those who have tried to come back from a significant knee surgery understand the undertaking that takes Zach is an I mean, he's a beast. Just I mean, he looks great. Um, it's not it's not easy to to kind of say like, all right, let's go, you know, so for him to have that courage to to say that and um, work through the things that he's worked through is uh, is just you can't do anything but tip your cap to him, you know. >> You said Bradford's a better version of himself than he was before the injury. Is there anything in particular you've seen from him through this >> I just like I just you know, normally a guy gets you know, is forced to go on IR it's a bummer, you know, and I know it and and it is for AB and I you could sense like there's frustration there cuz he wants to be healthy, he wants to be playing great football, but uh there's a way that you can approach that, too, and like the way he's approached it with positivity and energy, I think he's been a uh kind of a sense of like strength for the guys rather than someone that's um you know, that has to deal with the injury. So, just uh really really impressed by how he's handled everything. >> Uh you guys lost Robby Gould earlier in the year and obviously Brady Russell has filled in. They're different kinds of fullbacks. Uh the the signing today, is that an eye towards, you know, maybe a different type of fullback being added to the roster? >> Um I I wouldn't say it's a commentary on our on our current like abilities that we have. >> What does he bring uh >> Well, it gives us some more opportunity to be in two-back sets and even the stuff that Brady does out, you While you're not in two-back sets, but still being base, but we'll see we'll see how it goes. >> We didn't see Drew Lock when we were out there. Is he >> Um Drew was dealing with an illness today, yeah. He's here, though. >> Matt, I just want to I'm paraphrasing here. You talked about hey, we have to look at operations. Is that on the field or is it the process of getting whatever scheme you want on the field? >> Just a a lot goes into I mean, think about it, you get I don't know, on average 60-something opportunities to snap the ball a game on offense and defense. And uh those dictate you know, with special teams, you're looking at what 80 80-something you know. I don't know what the numbers are. It's not that many of snaps, okay? And so, it's like those are those are those are precious snaps. So, there's a lot of things that go into a lot of time and a lot of decision-making that goes into literally where everybody is lined up at all times and how you get there. And what they do. So, if you have if you understand how that works, you can understand that there's a lot that can be affected throughout that process to make what happens after the ball snap go in a certain direction. that's how that's how we choose to look at it. Um and that's not a commentary just on that's I mean, defensively, I mean, that's that's why we end up running the same thing every week. I mean, watch the tapes. They're like the same coverages. But how you deploy people, when you call it, how you get there, what you practice, you know, what information you give the players all week, how you get those players ready to play. I mean, all those things those are those those are chasing edges. Those are things that incrementally build throughout the week that ultimately, you know, you try to maximize that to give yourself the best chance to play the best football you can. So, I mean, that's what we're here all the time, you know. >> Back to the game, you guys were in shotgun quite a bit. Granted, there was a lot of like long distance situations, but what did you think of all the shotgun? Is that something you guys discussed over the weekend? >> Yeah, I think I think as a team we can be a we can do a better job of not being down multiple scores in the second half. Uh I think something that uh we've all talked about is like there's a time and place to kick into high gear and there's time and place to stay in our normal operations as well. So, um that's that's part of our part of the conversation. >> And uh Velus Jones, what did he give you in that game? >> Did a good job. There's there's um I think I think he can continue to have give opportunities for us to uh get him the ball, you know, the run and pass game. And uh leave it at that, but he's doing a good job, but there's definitely room for improvement. >> Back to Bradford, if you could think about how he was when you first got here and how he grew under John Benton, where's the biggest area of growth for him in three years? >> Well, I I I think uh I think it's a great example of just like look, we just we just coach everybody all the time. You know. John deserves a ton of credit with that and so does so does Anthony. About just a daily approach of just chipping away at becoming a a better version of yourself and a better player. And so um We've we've we've learned our lesson on that front and a lot of times in a good way. And it's paid massive dividends for us and it's been a learning experience for me of um you know, you don't just coach your starters, you don't just coach your starter, you coach everybody, man. You're We're always trying to develop guys. Even like even even today in our meetings, we're still talking about areas of growth and uh you know, in our defensive meeting, areas of growth where we can where we want to take it to the next level. That's individually and as a collective. And uh you know, we intend to continue that mentality because that's that's what works, you know, is that that constant growth. And so um JB and and AB are definitely two examples of that. >> We learned our lesson. What specific instance or just meaning that so many players had to play? >> I'm speaking from my personal experience of you know, you show up, you don't know a player. You make judgment about a player. It's like, what are you doing? Just coach the guy, you know, it's April, you know. Go go go coach the heck out of him and and see where he can go, you know, I've you I won't obviously say any names, but like there's we use that example all the time with our staff and when we meet and how we want to operate on a daily basis of like you know, quit making judgments about guys and why don't you just spend that energy coaching them up? >> Uh Drake Thomas, how's he doing? >> He's doing well. Uh no update for Drake, but um see him Wednesday. >> One of our national reporters is doing a story on two-point conversions when trailing by 14, you know, score touchdown to bring it to either to six or seven or eight. What's kind of your philosophy on that if you're willing to share? we have the history right now of what we do in those certain certain situation. Yeah, I probably won't. I'll let you find out our philosophy on it next time we're down 14 and we score a touchdown. >> Anything else? >> All right, thank you. >> Thank you. >> Thanks, Mike.
