Um just so it acted up too much in the game, couldn't go. We'll see how he feels this week. >> Just soreness. Does he need to have any more testing or anything? >> I don't believe so. I mean, when you have Achilles tendonitis like he does, it's um I mean, it's it kind of is what it is. I mean, I I hope it flared up tonight and I hope it he recovers throughout the week, but you don't think it's a longterm thing, but um right now it's it almost cost him this game and end up costing him two quarters and um hopefully he'll be able to play next week, but if not, we'll have to have the rest of the group step up and hopefully get him healed up by after the by-week. Now, you immediately think to next week because this is a week-by-eek league and the 49ers needed Mike Evans to play today to beat the Washington Commanders. They're down their top six wide receivers right now. So, I know there's a lot of talk about, oh, well, maybe Evans should have sat well and you probably would have had to been okay with a loss because they needed every ounce of production from Mike Evans to hold off Washington. They needed that lead because without him in the second half, the offense was not able to deliver. Three straight three and outs for the 49ers. And I don't think there's any team in the NFL that is winning down its top six wide receivers. So, this is going to be a weekly scrge for San Francisco to try to get as healthy as possible, as many capable bodies as possible in that receiver room to help unlock Brock Perie because he needs something. And today that something to close out the game had to come from the defense. Why don't we talk about Malik Mustafa first? >> Oh man, he hit the shutdown. I ain't going to lie to you. He really he really comes downhill. But that's what Malik's been doing. He's he showed that time and time again that he's he's not afraid to fill that gap and really make the play and in the biggest situations he showed up big time and time again. >> We got to the catch point. Uh just wanted to be physical at the point of attack and you know get that ball out. Hey in in that moment not thinking about anything but just getting a stop. So you know however however may unfolds is how how we get it done. >> One turf we're going to talk about Mustafa first or that pass rush but the 49ers pass rush. I mean they're doing special stuff. And if we were talking about next week how is this football team going to find what it needs to overcome its next opponent? That's the Atlanta Falcons who have a good rushing attack on the road next week. If they don't have Mike Evans, and I get that it's still technically an if at this point, but if they are down six of six top receivers again or five of six top receivers again, how are they going to have the efficiency to beat the Falcons? Well, maybe they get Nick Bosa back because you look at what this pass rush has done even without Nick Bosa and it is downright impressive. A 46% pressure rate for the 49ers today. Romelo Height 16% pressure rate. He is exploding off the football. Seemed that he might have ended this game multiple times for San Francisco, but obviously the penalty on Ashton Davis help prolong this game for Washington. Keon White has been awesome. And then Keon White, somebody who is in awe of what Malik Mustafa was able to do on the back end. >> Oh man, he hit the shutdown, man. You've got to remember that Malik was a star for the 49ers as a rookie in 2024. That was a dark year for San Francisco, but Malik Mustafa was a bonafide star. He was one of the best cover safeties in all football and he was a heat seeeking missile, which he is again here. Jeremy McNichols found out on the third down. And then one of the foranders guys in the locker room told me that Mal it was like Malik was climbing a tree to get up there and knock the ball away from Trayon Burks on the fourth down play. He is fully back from that torn ACL. And I think that safety position is truly benefiting from the fact that the 49ers again have a pass rush. Now, that pass rush is scheduled to get Nick Bosa back, which could give this defense yet another gear to where this defense can win games even if they don't have the first half outburst that they got from their offense. And the 49ers obviously built a big lead today when Mike Evans was available in the first half and the defense had just enough to finish it. You're talking about a wholly different defensive level, a stratospheric level if the defense can win games even without that outburst in the first half. And maybe, you know, as a championship team, as a team that is the Super Bowl favorite right now, when you look at the road moving forward, there might be a weather game. There might be an injury game, especially that given the way things are going for the 49ers with all those wide receiver injuries, there might be a time when your defense has to get it done wire towire. And maybe Nick Bosa is the added piece that allows the 49ers to do that. They could get him back as soon as next week. And then we can talk about how can the trade deadline further bolster some of the 49ers defensive hopes because I think that at both defensive end and defensive tackle, so both defensive line and at wide receiver, layering talent, especially given the injury rates in this league with this team is just what you have to do. 49ers were not thrilled with this win, nor should they be fully thrilled. >> Winning in the league is incredibly hard, so I'm always happy to win. But when you're up 20, I think we're up 20 to three and you can't shut the door in a team that has been struggling. I mean, if we were playing a super efficient team, I think we lose that game pretty easily. And like, we just can't have that. We're going to play there's we have more difficult games in our future. Like we have to what? Go to Kansas City. Like we have to play Seattle again. Anytime you play the Rams, Matt Stafford is Matt Stafford. Like there's there's teams out there that will take advantage of us going three and out multiple times. And our offense with our whether it's the players or our game plan, like I think it's too good for us to, you know, perform like that. >> I mean, I'm right there with my head coach. I feel like I've been around Kyle for so long. kind of adapted his kind of mindset like of his of it just being like one week is uh is its own situation and you know the emotions are fresh off of off of a game like that where I felt like that game should have never got to that point right it's just how high the standard is for us as a team and so um yeah I mean of course 6 and0 fantastic can't can't draw it up any better especially the fight that we had out there and on defense to be able to finish it out but um you know we're still going to continue to chase just progress ression like you don't want to just be a 6 and0 team. You want to be a team that's on the rise, right? Cuz the only thing that matters is being at your best when your best is needed later on in the season, right? And so finding ways to win while also finding ways to get better as a team overall, that's the goal. It's not just about winning. >> Just with the lead that we had and stuff, it's like, you know, put your foot on the gas pedal and and go make plays and put the game away kind of thing. Um and not put our defense in that kind of situation. You know, that's that's where my mind goes. But um you know at the same time you know it's the NFL man every single Sunday today Monday um it's you know it's a competitive game. You got the best players in the world in the sport playing and you just never know what can happen. So um yeah I'm obviously a little uh upset with how I finish the game and stuff but I know that moving forward like it's every single game matters when it comes down to playoffs and getting in and all the things. So um we'll take this dub as a team watch the film and um you know we got to be happy with it man. So, and we got a short week, so we do have a chance to get on the plane and go to Atlanta and and play better. >> I think Fred talking about this team needing to ascend instead of obviously descend over the course of this season. It's so important because we know the 49ers have already won their share of games. They're going to continue to win their share of games. They've got the best quarterback in football. Congratulations to Brock Perie. He now officially qualifies number one all time in passer rating. They've got a bunch of other good players on offense, even if the receivers are currently down. We we know that the 49ers are a winning outfit. We know that they're a winning team. But if they want to take this the ultimate distance, if they want to win a Super Bowl, you've got to peak at the right time. And that's where the leadership of somebody like Fred Warner comes in. You've got to make sure this is an ascending product as the season continues. And at this point, you know, it's impossible to to identify trajectory. The 49ers have these injuries they're fighting through. Wins are wins at at some level. I can put this perspective on it. In 2023, the 49ers started 5-0. The fifth win was against the Dallas Cowboys on this field at Levi Stadium. They suffered similar offensive weapon decimation in Cleveland in week six. And they lost to the Browns. They lost two more games to the Vikings and to the Bengals right here at Levi Stadium. So, they're 5-3 before they went on a run. Anyway, I think that 6-0 is better than 5- one, what it was in 2023. And one of the reasons why the 49ers have been able to get to 6 and0 they didn't get there with that veteran laden team in 2023 is because these young guys we can go back to the pass rush that that has surprised so much over the past 3 weeks but the young guys have given this team some juice to help them overcome even when the injury situation is such that that the 49ers probably shouldn't be undefeated. >> Yeah. Yeah. And I think um a lot of people talk about the experience we have, but I say it every week. I speak to those guys personally, but um we can't get where we want to go without the young guys. So um they they make up a great deal of our success. So um I I'm super happy with what they did in the draft. Those guys they got we got a bunch of steals in the draft. Like guy like Melo falling to the second round I think to me is absurd how polished of a pass rusher he is. I mean, Grayson in the fourth round, like, you know, um the the the front office did their job and I think we can't get where we want to go without those young guys playing as hard as they are. >> I was really impressed that Trent Williams knew what rounds that they were drafted in when he was just talking about that. I was like, how are you that aware of that? That's so weird. But besides that, you know, I'm just I'm I'm pumped for him. Um it's a young D line. I mean, we have got like four guys out there at a time sometimes and they're all in their first or second year and like that's awesome. Um, you know, one of my favorite stories is Sebass, Sebastian, you know, being a practice squad guy and getting the call up and going out there and making plays. Like, that's awesome. Grayson's playing at an incredibly high level. James is back. Uh, you know, he's just going to continue to get his legs underneath him. And then Romelo and Mikel, it's just I mean, it's so fun seeing Mike out there. Uh, cuz he's he is such a young talented player. It also messes me up that Romelo is like four years older than him and he's a rookie, but Mel's in his second year. That doesn't make sense. But I'm all for drafting older players because they understand the sense of urgency and they're all like adults. You're not dealing with like a 20-year-old. Nothing against Mikel for being a young guy, but like when you're 25, you kind of understand that. And so I think that is I was very happy that we drafted older players because they're all very ready for the moment. >> Trent also said that discussions of a Khalil Mack trade are above his pay grade. Not close enough to the decision makers in this building to know that much. But obviously the 49ers would welcome any reinforcements that they can get that would fit reinforcements that can fit that can help this team in a very pointed way. And even though the defense did close things out today, I don't think that Khalil Mack would hurt their ability to come in waves because there have been injuries. That doesn't mean that injuries will just stop though. Guys will come back, but that doesn't mean other guys won't get hurt. And I think that at both the defensive line and at wide receiver that rings very true. Let's talk a little bit about Brock Perie because I mean he was so so good for the first half plus of this game. I think even in the second half when things were starting to struggle for the 49ers because they were down so many receivers, they didn't have that separation. Pretty still almost pulled a rabbit out of his hat. There was an escape uh once where he got away from the pass rush, stepped up, nobody was open. KD was in double coverage. He still put the ball on George KD. Would have been a first down if KD been able to hold on to it, but obviously the physicality of the play. You don't really blame anybody, but the fact that the 49ers were out of firepower. Perie is at the very top of his game right now. You can feel it every single time he drops back. He sees the field. He senses where guys are. He senses where the pass rush is. Obviously, the Commanders got to him a couple times because guys weren't open downfield. That's going to happen if the 49ers are playing with a hand tied behind their back. But even with just Evans in that first half, Brock Birdie was able to make it work at an MVP level. And I mean, it is it is phenomenal. The the difference in efficiency in that first half was crazy. When you saw Pery at 0.56 EPA per play, Jaden Daniels who threw the ball away on fourth down, that was bad. It's hard to believe that people ever said that Jaden Daniels was better than Brock Birdie, but to Jaden's credit, he made some plays in the second half against that tired 49ers defense once they started leaking oil, but they got to him. They got to him plenty of times, enough to to win this game 2317. the trust that we've see from Shanahan and Pertie. You could see the pass rate over expectation by season in 2022 when Pertie first took over back when he threw the first of those 1500 pass attempts. They ran the ball more often. They have since passed more often than expected, over 5% more often than expected this year. That is a testament to not only Brock Birdie but also to Mike Evans and just to to the level that this 49ers pass game has reached when they have some semblance of health. That being said, some criticism I thought you know of those three three and outs. One of them Kyle Shanahan did not run the football and he had second and four after Perie ran on first down. You've got to put that ball on the ground. Don't fumble it like Christian McAffrey did today, but you've got to run the football to milk some of these leads when you are down. so many weapons. Now, in the third try, they tried to run the football to milk the lead, but they they couldn't get to the first down marker. So, I I just don't think they pick and chose their spots. They're like fish out of water, though, in a game where they're down so many receivers and the main part of the game plan, you're funneling every everything through Mike Evans is knocked out about halfway through. So, it was a tough situation and they needed the defense to bail them out and they did. Another point of concern and and Kyle Shanahan definitely concerned about this as well. The Eddie Pierro missed extra points. >> He's got to make them. So, I mean, he missed another one today and fortunately didn't get us, but um I think everyone knows the answer to that. You got to make your extra points. >> Already seven of them in a 49ers uniform. A season plus six games. Son Neil talked to him in the locker room. He did not see Luke McAffrey call for the fair catch there at the end. So, that's a tough one. And it looked like McCaffrey called it really really early. I'm going to have to go and watch the tape because I didn't see it on the TV copy. Tom, I'm going to rewatch all this. That aspect of special teams Neil is a really really good player. He could he was like a shark hunting there for for that tackle and he got it but they called the flag. The the two issues are the extra point miss and misses from Eddie Pierro and two Jacob Cowing. Kyle Shanahan also was critical of the decision. I mean, it's something we always got to take a look at, you know. I thought Jake made a real bad decision on the one. Um, I think he caught one on the four. I think it was from what I saw. So, I thought it was a bad decision. Had to let it go. Um, and I don't think he made a mistake in any any of the others. Um, but yeah, that was a bad decision by him >> to try to catch that football and then he muffed it, picked it up, and it hurt them in terms of field position and that drive didn't really get off the ground for the 49ers. So, they've got to get better in that special teams phase of the game. I don't think the numbers are going to be all too pretty once we see the final expected points, but they've got dudes on defense front end, back end. I know for Upton Stout who was dealing with a shoulder injury, it's not good right now. And and Ashton Davis was somebody who the Washington Commanders tried to pick on, but and I don't think it was the best game for Renardo Green. And I know that Washington lost Harry McLuren, who might have been a 49ers receiver reinforcement. That's that's too bad because we know that the 49ers have a good relationship with the Commanders trading wise, but boy, the 49ers stepped up when they needed to. Guys like Mustafa and then that defensive line stepped up when they needed to. Sometimes you need a gut check win and the 49ers got one. Why don't we hear from Brock Birdie and the rest of the 49ers? >> I mean, human nature thinks and and says like, you know, we got this game. But, you know, for me, I think the five years I've been in the NFL so far, like there's been a lot of games where you take a breath and you're on the sideline and you think, "Yeah, we got this." And so, for me, I don't know how what it looked like, but no, like this whole time, this whole game coming out at half, I'm like, "We got to we got to go put him away. We got to score." And and uh it's the NFL, dude. Like, Jaden Daniels is a great quarterback. He can bring this team right back. And sure enough, that's what he did. So, um, that's just sort of what's going through my mind is not trying to think for a second to take a breath. Like, what's my assignment on this next drive and where my mindset needs to be. Like, that's that's where I was probably trying to be. >> Winning's fun. >> Yeah, winning's fantastic. Um, you know, I hope Mike will be fine. It's just my gut intuition. I think he'll be great. Um, Deb will be back in a sec. Nick Bos will be back in a sec. So, I mean I mean every year you deal with injuries and it's like I mean yeah it sucks that guys get hurt because I love them but the league just rolls on. Hey, next Sunday you have another game, next Sunday you have another game. So just about doing what we can with the guys that are available and making plays >> when you can win and not play your best. Um obviously it's it's better than losing. Um but I know our standards high, you know, especially on offense. My standard's high. can't put the ball on the ground. But, uh, there's a lot of stuff we got to clean up, but it's always good when, you know, that's the case in a win. Uh, we all look at ourselves as young. Yeah. I mean, is there young energy, old energy, you know, every everybody has energy, >> you know, I don't I don't try to look, you know, compare years or anything like that. I think for us, it's uh one thing I love about this team is it's really just one one week, one day at a time. Uh, you know, we focus on controlling what we can control. You know, you see the narratives in the NFL in the offseason. we were we were nothing and too old and all these other things and all of a sudden we're 6 and0 and we're elite and all this stuff. So we we try to block out all the noise and just focus on every day getting better. Um correcting stuff we we need to correct and capitalizing on the stuff we're good at. And I think it's a sign of a mature football team um and the way that we practice, the way that we prepare and uh but you still got to go out there and play for three and a half hours. And so I like our mentality and our mindset. We just got to keep it that way. >> I feel good that we just won a game. I mean, 6 and0 is better than any other options in your record, but definitely um I mean, I feel good when the year's over and you're the last team to win the last game of the year. So, um I'll wait till that moment. >> That's a dog. He's a vet. He's been around the league for a long time and so he knows how to how to persevere and really uh push through. And so, he's been doing it his whole career and he's still doing it at a high level. >> Speaking of persevering, I want you to start persevering and pushing through. That's what this team's name has been able to do multiple weeks this season. Close game, still pulling it out at the very end. Speak to the resilience of this team. >> Um, I think it starts from the headman. Um, he he says it doesn't matter like next guy up and just play the next play and really really just persevere. Like I said, he preaches that uh he started off this season with a car and it was still out out there. And so if you can see that from him, then who am I to not give that the same energy to him? What can you say about all the young guys really stepping up in this situation? >> Yeah, I mean all the guys, Duggar, uh, Melo, Grayson, Kale, like they really are showing up and showing out this other season and the utmost respect for all of them cuz it's it's hard. They're doing a lot better than me my rookie year. Uh, so so much respect to them and I'm really proud of them. I'm not sure if you saw because you're rushing the pass there, but Malik's play on on Burks on this the fourth down on the second to last drive kind of climbed. Did you get a a glimpse of that play him climbing the ladder for the pass break? What was your view there? >> Oh man, he hit the up. I lie to you. He really he really comes downhill, but that's what Malik's been doing. He's he showed that time and time again that he's he's not afraid to fill that gap and really make the play and in the biggest situations, he's showed up big time and time again.

title: DeForest Buckner might want BACK to the 49ers...
text: Huge news pertaining to the 49ers this morning. I did not think a reunion with DeForest Buckner was possible until now. The Colts have fired their general manager Chris Ballard. And that means that Indianapolis might actually be willing to deal Buckner somewhere. Maybe back to the 49ers who are looking to build a super team. Maybe we shouldn't toss that around all too liberally, but the Rams can always take a little good trolling after their loss to the Cardinals. Buckner, 32 years old, he's making $13 million this year on base salary and he's still rushing the quarterback very, very effectively. 18 pressures already for DeForest Buckner this season. So, he still has some good football left. >> Sick and tired of the same summer dance every year. So >> and would obviously bring I think not only a pass rushing presence to the interior that the 49ers have rebuilt this year with Osa Deazua he's number seven in pass rush win rate OSA is but he's a stouter kind of lower to the ground figure DeForest Buckner at at 66 67 a very unique tall defensive tackle and obviously somebody you can move around the whole line that's what the 49ers did back when he was with them from 2016 to 2020 he's a good good unique ique player with his length and it would give the 49ers a total diversity of of sizes up front. But with 13 million on his contract for base salary this season, that is paid in pro-rated fashion. The Colts are two and four. That's why they fired Chris Ballard. That two-4 record uh means they've played six games, which means they've already paid DeForest Buckner for six games. That would mean that if you traded for him now, and I'm not saying it's going to happen this week. Uh, but it it it would only cost about 8.4 million for the rest of the season base salary right now. Every subsequent week, the the price tag comes down about 700 $750,000. I can't do all of that math all that accurately in my head, but it's about 7 to $800,000, we'll call it, cheaper every single week that the 49ers don't trade for DeForest Buckner. The 49ers have a lot of short-term cap space because they structured things that way to push expenses out to the future, but they have to watch their long-term salary cap situation. On top of the football, DeForest Buckner would definitely fit the 49ers culture because he's already fitted before. The the reason that he left and the first time is cuz he wanted a top of the market contract and the 49ers given the salary cap crunch given the fact that they were trying to build this as sustainably as possible for the future couldn't afford to give it. So, they told Buckner's agent back in 2020, you know, we can't match that price, but uh if you find it somewhere, come back to us and but make sure you come back to us with the offer of a first round pick. And and Indianapolis was very very willing to give up the first round pick. And obviously, the rest was history. The 49ers drafted Javon Kinlaw uh with that first round pick and obviously Kinlaw struggled to stay healthy for the 49ers. was never able to effectively replace DeForest Buckner and San Francisco has tried so hard to replicate the interior presence of Buckner over the years. They even signed Jayvon Hargrave for a ton of money. But Hargrave obviously also couldn't stay healthy for the 49ers. And uh they have been in a situation where I think finally this year they have been able to reapproximate the push up front that that they had back in the day. They're number three defensively right now. And they're doing it without Nick Bosa. And a lot of it's been because of Osa De Gazua and Grayson Halton, the rookie Sebastian Valdez, the second year undrafted free agents been big too. But if you add DeForest Buckner into that mix, then yes, you can start to talk about a super team defense. And here one thing, these teams are not built on paper, right? The Rams are learning that the very, very hard way. So many thought that they would just waltz their way to a Super Bowl win because uh they collected some impressive names, but it's not working out on paper. There's a lot of garbage yardage that cohesion between the units is not what it should be. Obviously, Miles Garrett's on the shelf right now for the Rams. The one thing about DeForest Buckner, you add a premium piece to what the 49ers have already, you already know that he fits. you already know that the cultural fit into the building is there based on the fact that he played for you and played under this regime in the past and I think that's very very important. So anybody who you add you have to make sure that they're going to fit within the ecosystem of the team and be a productive addition. Other possibilities and yesterday was a really good day for the 49ers. Everything seems to be coming up ners right now by the way. yesterday. As far as teams who uh lost, who might be trade sellers, like the 49ers saw a lot of things break in their favor. For example, Tampa Bay blew a lead to Pittsburgh and lost. Tampa Bay has not only Vea, and we've talked a lot about him, and that you don't really need to explain why Vava would make your football team better. He's somebody who could pass rush from 350 pounds, and he grew up in Milpedas next to Levis's. Uh Vava is on the Bucks and they're one and five. But they also have a player named Aan Robinson who's a big big run stopper. Not as big as Vava, but Interior fire hydrant, more of a run stopper, but he has played under Raheem Morris. That was back for the Rams. And I think it's somebody who Morris likes and and Aan would probably come cheaper than Vivea. He's on a $10 million contract this year. So you trade for him around mid-season, you only owe 5 million for somebody like Aan Robinson. And then of course the Chargers are 0 and6. And this is a different position. This is defensive end. Khalil Mack is essentially a pure edge rusher. Has the ability to to drop at at age 35. But you're probably not going to run Mack as a run stopping defensive tackle. But the 35-year-old future Hall of Famer, Khalil Mack, is on the Chargers making $18 million this year. So, he cost a pro-rated amount of of that. Uh, I would think that the Chargers uh would be in sell mode here very very soon. They lost to the Chiefs yesterday. So, those are just some names to watch, but Devor Buckner might top the list, especially this morning with the Colts firing Chris Ballard. Insane stat here. The Colts have had Ballard as long as John Lynch has been the GM of the 49ers and never once have the Colts won a divisional title in his stretch as GM. Now, last year they started I think they started 8 and2. They had a very good record to begin the year. They went all in. They traded for Sauce Gardner a couple first round picks and then they decided to reward Daniel Jones this past off season with a contract extension despite the fact that he was coming off of an Achilles tear. And obviously the Achilles tear really really hurt the Colts last year. But pushing the chips into the middle of the table ended up being the undoing of the Chris Ballard tenure in Indianapolis. Crazy to me though. I mean, think if John Lynch had not won a single division title in 10 years for the 49ers. I think fans should have some perspective. Lynch is maybe the best GM in the league. And there are some 49ers fans who don't have the perspective to realize that. Maybe the firing of Chris Ballard and the fact that he hasn't won a single title in 10 years for the Indianapolis Colts should put that into the proper framework. Now, the Colts, they lost yesterday to the Tennessee Titans. When you lose the Titans at home, bad things can happen as far as firings go. And well, Deorest Buckner wasn't very happy about it. So, where does this go from here? We'll find out. For the 49ers, we know where this goes tonight. Brock Pery will become the NFL's all-time passing efficiency leader on Monday Night Football, which is in just a few hours. He needs five more attempts to reach 1500 and officially qualify for the career leaderboard where he will be number one in several categories. Caught up with Trent Williams in the locker room a couple days ago. I haven't played this for you guys yet. So, here's some pregame material ahead of 49ers commanders. Remember Trent Williams? The 49ers traded with Washington for big Trent. So, we talk about bringing DeForest Buckner back. The reason that Trent Williams is a San Francisco 49er is because they traded with the team whom they play tonight. >> Sometime I forget that I even played even though I've been here going on what seven years. So I only played nine seasons there. It was there 10 years played nine seasons. You know I'm just as spent almost just as much time here as I have there. >> Maybe 10 years here. >> I don't know. [laughter] That that was when you met Kyle, right? Your first interaction with Kyle in Washington. >> Um, >> thinking back to that, what were your first impressions of Kyle? Do you remember those back? >> Yeah, I I just it was uh my first time ever being around a coach of any sort um that was that close to my age that wore Jordan shorts or Jordans that you know like laidback and cool. It was like, >> you know, back then coaches, you had you had to a right of passage you had to go through and most of the time you got to have your own room or coordinator job, you were, you know, mid to late 40s. And you know, that's kind of how all the coaches looked around that time. Having Kyle being a young kind of like a breath of fresh air, you know, in the midst of his dad who was very very old school, you know, we had Bobby, you had a lot of coaches that was very old school. Then you had Kyle who was kind of like, you know, cool the other side of the pillow. title: Coach McCarthy Press Conference (Week 7 at New Orleans Saints) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: Good afternoon everyone and welcome to the UPMC Rooney Sports Complex on the South Side. Bob Pompeani here with Missy Matthews. It's a victory Monday for the Steelers after they came back from down 13 in the fourth quarter to win yesterday 6 or 26 to 19. They had to do it in overtime though, Missy. It was one of those games that at one point you're thinking, "Oh, how are they going to dig themselves out of this?" And the next thing you felt like it was going to turn in their favor. >> Yeah, 13-point deficit as you said tied for the fifth largest comeback in Steelers history. You have to go back to uh 1992 to kind of get close to one and the rest are, you know, a while away. But, um yeah, it was something to see for sure. I will say I really believe as Coach McCarthy said the Steelers fans took over that stadium. Um it felt more like a home game and maybe that's why it worked since the Steelers are undefeated at home. >> Yeah, I if you had to put it on a percentage 50/50 or more than that for Steelers fans? >> Definitely 50/50. Um you definitely could feel the Tampa Bay fans and you saw the red, but when it came time uh for the Steelers defense to, you know, ask the crowd for noise that the towels were everywhere. It wasn't just like patches of towels. >> No question about it. This is the Mike McCarthy press conference brought to you by PNC and thank you for joining us here on KDKA Plus and all the Steelers digital platforms here as we get set for Mike's press conference uh on a week where the Steelers uh will end up going to Paris to play a game against New Orleans. We're going to get into that in a little bit and all the ramifications that come with it, but first you know, Aaron Rodgers first three quarters it looked like they had his number and for that matter the entire Steelers offense. And all of a sudden things changed in the fourth quarter when he put together some amazing drives. Third and 10 completions, long plays that kept drives alive and resulted in this game going the other way. >> Yeah, it definitely was one of those ones where the player said, you know, they were going to play out the game and see what happened. It kind of felt like it was such a big hole. How were you going to get out of it? Uh continuing to go three and out for the Steelers offense, it just felt discombobulated compared to what we saw last week. But, I do think as Aaron said after the game, they started getting DK Metcalf involved more and it seemed to really help things with the offense. >> Yeah, and in overtime, Rodgers goes six for seven for 51 yards. Fourth quarter and overtime combined, 17 for 22. So, he got hot at the right time as he often does. And he incorporated, as you said, DK Metcalf who had 11 catches. But, it's been impressive to watch him even if he doesn't get the numbers he wants and the stats that people want. He's still involved and he made a beautiful block on the Jermaine Kearse touchdown. >> Yeah, definitely a team player. And you can see that this team plays for each other even on defense. Just the excitement for, you know, Jaylen Everett getting his first interception. Even Jamal Dean being able to do it against his former team. Jaylen Ramsey just completely, you know, shutting it down at the end, literally running with teammates straight to the locker room. That's, you know, it's it's definitely a tight unit, a tight team and it's good to see. And now you stacked wins, you got the road win. Now, let's, you know, see how many more you can stack. >> Two more against teams they should be favored to beat coming up before their bye week. I want to talk a little bit more about Bernard as we watch McCarthy here and and just the role he's playing because there are a lot of injuries, obviously. So, there aren't that many healthy bodies. Both the Brandons got involved, but they really weren't involved. It came down to Aaron Rodgers trusting the rookie and boy, that trust seems to have increased each week. >> And it kind of has to, right? But, I think you saw glimpses of it throughout training camp when Michael Pittman and DK Metcalf weren't practicing. So, Aaron getting some one-on-one time and it seems like from what everyone has said, Bernard is he wants to be taught. He wants to learn from Aaron. He wants to go over things. He wants to continue getting better. And you can see as you said each week it keeps happening. You saw the rookie mistake not getting that fourth down conversion earlier in the game. But then the way he was able to kind of shed that tackler, reach out, get into the end zone for that touchdown. That that was that was big. As you said, DK Metcalf helped. But I think for a rookie to have that spatial awareness and also to you know, do it in such a clutch time. That's that's an easy thing to learn from. And that's good. >> The run game didn't produce many yards, but they had some hard runs. And we saw the return of Rico Dowdle who's coming off that toe injury. And I think his role had to be established and it was. Maybe not to the tune of what people would have expected cuz Jaylen Warren didn't get as many touches as Dowdle in the first half. But he was on the field more. He had like 57 snaps. Dowdle didn't have that many. I think it's important that he got involved and he did get involved. I also like the fact that they were both on the field at the same time. We haven't really seen too much of that. That's an interesting dynamic for a defense to try to figure out. >> Yeah, absolutely. We even saw Riley Nowakowski involved a little bit specially there towards the end of the game. It did feel though that the the offense was a little clunky. Even at halftime coach McCarthy said he felt like the interception just really got them off balance. They weren't able to run the ball and do what they wanted to do. So hopefully, you know, you can you can learn from a win which is a good way to learn instead of from a loss and we can see improvements with Rico in more of a defined role and also as you said, you fed Jaylen so much in these past few games. We've seen the success AFC player of the week for him for offense. You need to continue doing that as well. >> Defensively, honestly, I have to say this too. Tampa's one and five for a reason too. They make mistakes. And realize they don't have their starting quarterback Baker Mayfield makes a big difference. Although I thought Daniels played very well especially in the first half. However, they missed an open Ebuka on what would have been a a touchdown. It would have been 17 nothing instead of 13 at halftime and then Trotter drops what surely would have been a pick-six. But the Steelers took advantage of that. Once they made those mistakes, then they paid for those mistakes. >> What goes around comes around, right? I felt like, you know, the the Steelers defense stepped up in opportune times. I think, you know, we talked about Jaylen Ramsey at the end. Even you have to go back to the beginning. Keanu Benton came into that game with his hair on fire, looking to prove something or to show people, "Hey, look over here, too." Nick Herbig finally getting a sack. He ended up with two on the day. It It felt like there were pockets of the splash plays that we're used to seeing from that defense. And hey, when it counted, they made it count. >> I often wonder hair on fire came from. But I imagine if your hair was on fire, you'd play the way you played, right? So, it makes sense. >> start tackling everybody. >> It was crazy to hear that. All right, let's talk about other guys on that defense because they played well. I thought Payton Wilson, the more I watch him, the more I think he's going to be just a tremendous inside linebacker. Every week you look at the stats, Missi. 11 tackles, eight solo, 13 tackles, seven solo. He's always involved. >> Yeah. And I Jaylen Ramsey up there, too, with the the double digits tackles, as well. And it it's good to see that I feel like the move of Patrick Graham from up in the booth down to the field was very necessary and I think it's paying dividends, for sure. Just the communication that you're seeing amongst all levels of the defense with the defensive coordinator and then the specific unit coaches. It's very apparent that it is getting everybody on the same page. There's not, you know, the game of telephone of players saying something to somebody who has a headset, then saying it to Patrick Graham. It's all very um tighten it now. >> Yeah, exactly. And I think, you know, if you look at these games, too, the one thing you take away, the NFL has seen the return of the running back in many ways. Guys who are putting up big numbers. Last week the Steelers silenced Jonathan Taylor, who was arguably one of the best. And Bakari Irving yesterday had no room. He was almost similar statistics, less than 50 yards rushing. He came off a performance in Dallas where he had like 100 and 55 yards rushing. So, when you stop that, especially with a young quarterback, you're putting an awful lot of pressure on him. All right, Mike McCarthy's just entered the press conference room. Let's take you there now live. >> Mike, what can you say about Jalen Ramsey and just him embracing his role and how he was corner his whole career and then, you know, the way that they're utilizing him here so far? >> I mean, Jalen Ramsey, just a multi-dimensional player. You can play him anywhere in the back. I really appreciate not only his ability, but his, you know, his football intelligence. The jumping in out of positions. Obviously, the sack into the game was exactly how you draw it up, you know, as far as the technique of both T.J. and Alex, you know, setting that edge and for him to come, you know, just the the timing, the whole the whole the whole process of it, you know, and that's what, you know, these veteran guys give you. And you know, Jalen exemplifies that. >> Mike, any concerns with what's going on in Paris disrupting your schedule, your itinerary, and has the team made any adjustments in terms of security, etc.? >> Well, I'm obviously very aware. I mean, that's that's part of the normal planning, you know, anytime you you go, you know, go abroad. So, and that's no different with this particular opportunity to play in Paris. So, I mean, the team is excited about playing, you know, over there. But yes, I mean, we're in contact with the league. We had a Zoom call today with the league office, you know, which is the normal protocol before you go over there. So, it was with the whole team. So, you know, we feel like we have a really good plan. We're we're aware of you know, the situations over there and uh have have a lot of confidence in our plan. >> Mike, has there been any discussion about maybe a contingency if things were to escalate maybe talk to the league anything like that. >> I know the league is you know put out you know statements on this I know they're updating we have people over there as we speak and you know like I said we we we have a plan and I haven't been part of those discussions. >> Mike the Saints are already over there you guys aren't going over until later in the week. What what kind of went into that thought process and how do you plan on what challenges are waiting >> I think just like anything you know when the schedule comes out you know we're on a 7-day week you know flow here you know which playing yesterday in Tampa you know the travel back you know that factors into it we play again 7 days later you know against Cleveland so that all the all those factors go go into this so you know whether you're playing in the Super Bowl or you're playing in a Monday night Monday night game that's you know more than 5 6 hours you know in the air you mean you look at all those things and the reality of it is I've always just try to stick to the basics you know the hydration the sleep and and just to make sure you give the give the men the best opportunity to you know to prepare to perform and then ultimately stay in as normal of a flow of preparation as you can so I you know we we looked at both options and we clearly feel that this this one of leaving Thursday is the best one for us. >> Mike have you talked to the team personally about you mentioned the zoom call have you talked to them personally about their concerns anything you want to tell them about going over to Paris and their concerns? >> Absolutely that's really what today's team meeting was for. You know we had the zoom call with the with the league office obviously you know Mr. Rooney was in there and so chance to ask questions and then I went through the whole plan you know everything that we foresee happening throughout the week as far as our schedule and the adjustments that we need to make and so forth. But uh you know, it's just not one conversation. It's a continuing conversation. >> Mike, is there a point in the season where rookies stop being rookies? >> Yeah, I hope it was yesterday. So, yeah, that'd be that'd be great. No, I I I do I'm proud of our rookie class. These guys are you know, and they're getting they're getting some opportunities early. So, I think what Jeremy did yesterday was outstanding. He was the game ball winner on offense. So, that that speaks volumes of how everybody feels about, you know, where he is and his climb and his contribution to the offense. So, yeah, definitely. It's it's it's it's it's something that you know, it's been like this for, you know, two decades. Your young your young players have to play and I think when they do have opportunities early, uh it's very beneficial. Uh my personal experience has been your younger players are probably going to be, you know, playing a bigger role in November, December. That's that's how uh you know, the some of these seasons I know have gone for me personally. Um and you look at our IR situations, you know, we're even of late with injuries. So, it's important for our young players to step up. >> Mike, you mentioned that IR situation. Do you anticipate DeShawn being able to fully return this week and play Sunday against us? >> Well, I hope so. I thought he had a great week last week. So, you know, those are the conversations that we're having. >> Mike, Aaron Rodgers postgame he thought it was a trajectory-altering win for you guys being able to come back. How do you feel those type of wins where maybe you don't play your best or have a comeback late impact a team during the season? >> Yeah, I I think anytime you win a football game on the road and you don't feel like you played above the standard that that you set out to play, that's uh there's a lot of value uh in that win because that directly points to the the potential for high adversity in the game, which we we had plenty of. Um I think our fans did a phenomenal job pulling us through there at the end. I mean, the fourth the the second half particularly was felt like a home game. Um so, that was that that was great to see. But, you know, the defense kept us here, you know, just, you know, keeping them to field goals. And then, you know, once we got got going on offense and got the ball spread around, you know, it was it was a big challenge. That's a good defense schematically and personnel. And you know, Todd's done it for a long time. So, it's an excellent win on the road. >> Aaron's been been part of a lot of a lot of games, but how important is it for young guys that get those opportunities when, you know, a game it seems like the other team has and then you guys have to fight back and follow away. Teachable moment for a lot of the young guys you have on the team. >> Yeah, I mean, there's nothing there's nothing better than personal experience. I mean, it's it's it's what you value the most as as a football team. Um you can show videos, you can have all the educational conversations, um examples, but to go through it together and to go through it in real time. Um to be able to take the day and correct it and and, you know, correct the things that you know you could do better, need to do better, and still come out of it with a win. That's that's a good place to be. >> Is your time to kind of take a step back and look back at the game? Um offensively, are there things that you wish that you had done or could do in the future moving forward to kind of jump-start you guys a little bit earlier? >> Uh we put a lot of time and energy in starting the game. So, uh I think just like anything, I'm a big believer in, you know, return on investment, you know, ROI. So, when we don't start very well, I I do I take it very personal. So, but at the end of the day, I know what the process is. I know the benefits of it. I know I know what it I know what it looks like. And, you know, and that's why you it's it's it's so important to evaluate on Mondays. You know, Mondays are very important. Yeah, it's the most important video you watch of the week. You know, we spend so much time talking about the other guy. You got to make sure you're talking about yourself, you know, and that's clean your own house. Just make sure we get that part right. That's self-scout. You know, you do it every you do it all the time. So, we did that again today. Don't want to alarm anybody, but it's so Um and it was good. It was healthy. >> In cleaning your house and that self-scout, you talked about third and two to third and six a few weeks ago. How have you guys seen progress in third down? What do you need to do to keep seeing progress in third down? >> Well, third one and six this week. I mean, you know, we Well, we left we left some out there and that's where, you know, we'll actually you know, we'll start that a little early tonight. Um you know, we have to convert on third downs. I think it puts us in a different different level offensively cuz that's can answer. You know, we got about four or five set sets of downs that we left out there, you know, yesterday. So, and I still had a lot of, you know, opportunities, you know, definitely want to get the ball ran more. Um that that's that's clearly a focus. But yeah, the third down is is it's it's it's it's happened, you know, it's a numerous weeks, and so we got to do a better job there, but we're doing the first part pretty good, you know, we're we're the create the third down opportunities we're creating are are where you want to be. >> Mike, what did you see from the young receivers who came up from practice squad, and do you feel like with Pittman and Roman out you need some other options at receiver? >> Well, I think the biggest thing is you you know, you just continue to develop. I I I you're probably tired of hear- hearing this. I know Omar is, too. I I I believe in the 68 guys that we have in the building, and when opportunities are presented, that's that's who I prefer to go with, and but I'm not blind or naive to, you know, the others peop- the men that are out there, especially if you work with individuals in the past and have a past relationship here and so forth. So, uh so, you you you're always looking, and that's that's Omar's job, and and in our our our personnel department does a good job of it, but yeah, I thought both Brand- both Brandons did some good things, you know, so this They just got to keep working, you know, these guys have they've busted their tail, you know, they've earned this opportunity, so we'll just continue to work. >> Mike, after the game you said that you felt like the practice preparation over the last 2 weeks has been what you wanted it to look like. When we talked to some players in the locker room this morning, they kind of reiterated that point. Payton Wilson saying he feels like the Thursday padded practices have really been beneficial, have really been something good. Have you changed anything or is this just the part of a team getting to this point in the season, finding that cohesion? >> I'll tell you clearly it's it's where we are in the season. title: THE FASTEST GIRL IN SOMALIA Bonus: Minneapolis
text: I'm in a gym in Minneapolis with producers Becca and Cara. It's December 2025 and the snow is coming down outside. In here though, it's warm and the energy is high. All around us are members of the Somali community in the Twin Cities using weights, stretching, and getting coached by Optif. >> Abdi is leading a bunch of cardio exercises. He's starting each one off with one multiple times in a row, so nobody really knows how many reps they're actually doing. Through the leg kicks and the jumping jacks, people are laughing and joking. >> Abd has traveled the globe in his running and coaching career. But it's here in Minneapolis, home to the largest Somali community in the US, that I can see the impact that he's making in real time. Now in his 60s, Abdi is fully focused on training the next generation. At this point, he told us he's taken thousands of people under his wing as a coach and mentor. In warmer months, he coaches people for races outside. And then when it's too cold to run, he leads gym classes like this one multiple times a week, bouncing between different venues, age groups, and skill levels. From high school track athletes to excited grandmas. [music] I don't care how good the person is, how talented the person is. Is really what's more important is, you know, if the person is dedicated and have the passion and doesn't matter how far you go, but just you do your best. >> It's in this gym with Abdi where I could imagine a different outcome for Seamya. one where she's living among her peers from the diaspora, among other people who have also traveled a great distance. In this alternate reality, Samya is still running, [music] still training. I can picture her in this room with us, doing all these non-stop reps. I bet she'd even be making jokes about how bad my form is each time I did a lunge. >> [music] >> Honestly, she'd most likely be in front of the class with Abdi demoing how to do it right. The Seama I knew would still be [music] pushing the people around her to keep moving forward, to keep striving towards something, even if they didn't know what the next step would [music] bring. But of course, Simeia never had that chance. [music] If Samia were alive and training today back home, do you think her circumstances would be different? >> No, she didn't have any chance to begin with [sighs] because that was the system. The system that failed her that time still exists. >> Seama's story has become a rallying cry for many [music] athletes I've spoken with who are demanding more from Somali leadership. Protection, accountability, and a real commitment [clears throat] to train professional athletes. Abdi told me this too. [music] In the years since Samya died in 2012, he says he's been waiting to see meaningful progress for athletes within [music] Somalia, but so far he hasn't seen any. That's what has never happened and it's not still happening and it's not going to happen anytime soon the way it is. [music] When it comes to international competitions, Somalia continues to lag behind. At the most recent summer Olympics in Paris in 2024, [music] only one athlete represented the country. He didn't medal. But at a grassroots level in Moadishu, things are looking a little better. It's becoming common to see kids play soccer along the city's beautiful beach. [music] Fans are openly celebrating athletes again, and club sports are emerging. [music] It's more reminiscent of the days when Abdle was coming up. But at the same time, girls and women still face danger when participating in sports, [music] including death threats. And people are still leaving Somalia every day in search of a better [music] life. Some of them have landed here in Minneapolis like Muhammad who stopped to talk to us in one of Abdi's gym classes. As people were chatting and milling around the room, he told us how Abdi has helped him build his life here. For me, I actually grew up in a refugee camp and I grew up hearing about the story of Abdi. Basically he was the guy who went to America and conquered the world because he became a champion within such a short short period of time. So living in a refugee camp it was more if he can do it so can I regardless of my circumstances. Muhammad came to the US on a scholarship but soon started to wonder if staying was worth it. He was homesick and struggling and then a friend gave him Abdi's number. He called not expecting Abdi to even pick up. And then the next day the guy just shows up on my door like legitimately and I remember like going crazy. Imagine the greatest athlete in the history of your country coming to visit you. >> Abdi showed up on Muhammad's doorstep and from that day on Abdi became a mentor for him. >> I never used to run actually but then after getting to know him I ended up running for college. It's like every day sort of um I get to leave with with a legend. >> Muhammad is just one of the many people who Abdi is looking out for. And as the legendary runner drove us around Minneapolis for the weekend, from one workout class to the next, it became clear how much he really truly cares. As we drove, we started to talk about something new that was hitting the community hard. The ICE raids. That December, customs and immigration agents descended upon the Twin Cities. They publicly targeted the Somali community, throwing them into the national spotlight. In the car, without our microphones on, Abdi told us about the fear that many Somali were feeling. how many people were starting to avoid being out in public. People who'd built their lives and families here, who in some cases had sacrificed everything to get here in the first place, were now worried about stepping outside. But despite all of this, Abdi stuck to his usual schedule. >> He parked the car and we followed him into a complex of apartment buildings. In a recck room upstairs, another group was waiting to start their workout. This class was for older Somali women. As they started arriving, we arranged chairs in a big circle. Abdi pulled out a bag of resistance bands for all of us to use. Chatter filled the room as people stretched and caught up on each other's lives. >> She become a grandmother. >> Wow. Amazing. Okay, we're going to do the squat. >> Okay, get this. Get this. Get this. Split it out. Split it on. Splice it on. >> Together, we did squats and arm raises and other exercises. And again, Abdi did his signature count off. >> As Abdi counted, some of the women started to sing, riffing along with the numbers. 300 15. >> This is a really important group for Abdi. Some of them are still adjusting to life here in the US. >> This adult group is is really for the health our community. Uh we came from a nomadic society. We're walking you is it's normal to walk. And now when we just come to this country you know sitting too much sedentary the food changed everything's changed culture change. So even those ladies just to explain to them you know just come out of the house let's just exercise let's just walk. So I'm just trying to transform the the whole community and uh you know just promote healthy and wellbeing and wellness and that's what it's all about. >> When we were in Minneapolis, we knew that ICE arrests were starting to happen, but we were still learning how many Somali would be affected and where they would be sent. [music] Later, we heard that the week we were there, ICE detained a Somali man named Adam Abdullah, who was living legally in the Twin Cities. [music] After 9 months in detention, he was ultimately sent to Guantanamo Bay before being deported back to Somalia. [music] His criminal record, two parking tickets. All around us, arrests like this one were happening. And it was only the beginning of a whole winter of violence and fear and uncertainty. [music] That uncertainty didn't go away when we were in these workout classes with Abdi, but it faded into the [music] background. Something else was more present. It was the feeling of a community coming together under this one roof to get up and move. >> I thought again about Simeia, the energy and joy that she brought to [music] running and her drive to just keep moving forward no matter what was going on around her. Even on days when it felt too dangerous to go outside, [music] she kept moving one rep at a time, one foot in front of the [music] other. text: Joining us now, ladies and gentlemen, is a man who is commissioner of a league that is tipping off today. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, SGA, he can become only the fourth player to win three straight Kia. I don't know if it always is always this. Kia NBA MVP awards. Victor Wembanyama, he can become the first player to lead the NBA in blocks per game in four consecutive seasons since blocks became an official stat in 1973. >> Wow. >> Magic happening all across the association. League-wide, there's storylines and it feels like there's hope more than ever before. The commissioner of the NBA, ladies and gentlemen, Adam Silver. >> You know, Pat, I wasn't sure if you'd be able to read my handwriting. >> Yeah. Well, I'll tell you what. Just like everything else, very efficient and fantastic. Thank you for sending this via carrier pigeon. Now, um let's talk about your league and some of the stats that we just read off there. How do you feel about the state of the league where we're at and what do you expect from this particular season? More parity from your league's best? >> Absolutely. Again, you you rattled off some of those great stats about the number of champions, unique champions, eight different over the last eight seasons, but I can't remember a season that was so anticipated in terms of the level of competition across the league. Tonight is the late game, you know, after the the Knicks are opening at home for the ring ceremony with with LeBron. Um we got Boston and we got uh Detroit this afternoon. I mean, that's I think as I look across the league, there's something to watch on every on on every club, like a bunch of new young stars. Um and as I said, I think the parity is working. Combination of so much new talent in the league, I think a good agreement with the Players Association that um allows, you know, for players to be well distributed around the league. So, I you know, again, as I said, I I don't remember a season and and then I I should add, you mentioned it, you know, we changed the rules around the lottery. So, there's there's zero incentive to lose. You know, what I'm what I'm saying to our general managers in the past, at a show like this in the beginning of the season, people would have been looking at statistics on where you stand and what that means for your lottery odds. No math required this year. Just go out and win. >> I like that you did that. I like that you take a stand. You do evolve a lot as a league. I think if you see a problem, you try to address it quickly because you know the state of the league is the most important, and you guys have a massive media rights deal looking to take advantage of all the properties that you're on. What are some of the changes this season that we should get used to seeing? Is there anything that I saw there were some You went into the sports gambling a little bit, which I know you have been very very very active about since the beginning of it all with your league. You understand that society is going to do sports gambling. It has been happening for a long time, but now we're at a state of everybody having access to it and doing it. You've been trying to curtail it so it protects the league, its players, and its fans. What have you done this year? I feel like this is a big step for you guys actually and for the future of gambling as a whole with leagues. >> So so, you know, frankly we're trying to have more control over the kinds of bets that are placed. And to your point, I mean it's it's so widespread at this point, putting aside when it used to be illegal in most places, but still was widespread. You know, our view is we'd much rather have regulated transparent sports betting than illegal underground sports betting, which is what the old framework was. And so, now you have essentially 40 states that have legalized sports betting. You have these prediction markets now, technically called, you know, contracts, but I think in in effect at least the impact on the league is the same in terms of people making wagers on what's happening on the floor. And you have a global market of sports betting on top of that. I think that gets left out of the conversation sometime that even if we change the regulations in the US, you have at least 80 other countries in the world where you can take place bets on NBA games. So, ultimately the goal for the league is to protect our integrity. And one of the things we've worked with on the operators is limiting certain kinds of bets, the ones that are easiest to manipulate. And I think we're frankly, and we see this in all sports, where guys maybe are are are are screwing around a little bit, but they don't think it's going to have any impact on the on the outcome of the game. It has a core impact on our integrity, but for example, the first step bets. You know, they had some issues in other sports around first pitches and things like that. In our league, it could be who scores the first basket or who who's the first assist, who's the first rebound. Things that arguably would have no impact on the outcome, but something which would go to our core integrity if guys are screwing around. So, in working with the operators, we said, "Take those kind of bets just just off the table so that we don't have to think about that stuff. Take the kinds of bets where you have two-way players who are just coming through the league where they don't have the same incentives as as journeyman players, as guys on under full contracts who who who might be tempted to screw around. Issues, bets around unders, which are the easiest to manipulate. A guy's going to have a under eight assists, you know, under 12 points. You know, so I I I think there's I'm pro regulation in this area. I Again, it sports betting is here to stay. It's cuz it's global. Fans love it, frankly. There's enormous engagement around it. There's problem gambling. We have to worry about that. And then we have to focus on the integrity of what happens on the court. >> I like that you're playing defense against it instead of just either being oblivious or acting like somebody else is going to take care of it or somebody else will figure this out. The government laws will figure You're playing actual defense. I respect you doing that. You are a forward-thinking commissioner. I think you have to be with the NBA, especially with the demographic of your fans, which is younger. You have to be able to reach them all. You've said that you try to do that. I think you creating things of importance that you can market and sell, like your Jackie Moon, I think is a big deal, too. And we're a big fan of that NBA Cup.
